criteria.rationale: The deliverable accurately reflects all source constraints, operative authority rules, and arithmetic relationships. By inspecting the workspace registry and records in the tool trace, the strategy rightly enforces the approved 21-calendar-day notice from record-17.txt and rejects the unapproved 84-day draft in record-22.txt. All stated quantities (800 sets/month demand, 1,500 normal and 2,500 ramp units/month capacity, ~25-day tooling transfer, 3–4 months plastic redevelopment, and 4–5 months parallel electronics redevelopment) match the request. The bridge and 21-day capacity calculations (4,000 sets for 5 months, 4,800 sets with a 1-month contingency, 560 sets consumed in 21 days on a 30-day basis, and 1,750 sets produced at 2,500 sets/month leaving 1,190 net sets or ~1.5 months) are mathematically sound and appropriately qualified regarding the unit-versus-set distinction. The document separates proposed negotiation terms from existing entitlements and makes no unauthorized commitments.

evidence.source_quote:
record-17.txt: revision 2; approved 2025-06-20; status in force; approved by process owner.
record-22.txt: revision 3; created 2025-06-23; status draft; not approved.
evidence.output_quote: Plan against the approved 21-calendar-day cessation notice; no extension is agreed. The newer 84-day draft is not operative. At 800 sets/month, a 4–5-month electronics development cycle cannot fit inside this notice.

evidence.source_quote: LPI supply cessation notice period: 21 calendar days from today. No extension has been agreed.
evidence.output_quote: Plan against the approved 21-calendar-day cessation notice; no extension is agreed. The newer 84-day draft is not operative.

evidence.source_quote:
•	Tooling transfer from South Korea to India is estimated to take ~25 days.
•	ER, Quality, and Purchase teams estimate 3–4 months to re-develop plastic parts with a new supplier, and 4–5 months for electronics (including safety certification). These can proceed in parallel.
•	Modlev’s current monthly demand is 800 tail lamp sets.
•	LPI has capacity of 1,500 units/month and can ramp up to 2,500 if required.
evidence.output_quote: Planning illustration: five months at 800 sets/month requires 4,000 sets; one extra month adds 800, giving a 4,800-set gross bridge target before deducting usable inventory and confirmed receipts. Using 30-day months, 21 days consumes about 560 sets. Only if 2,500 units/month means complete sets and ramp-up is immediate would 21 days produce about 1,750 sets, leaving roughly 1,190 above concurrent demand—about 1.5 months, not a full bridge.

criteria.consequence: None; executive decision-makers receive accurate baseline figures, valid authority determinations, and properly bounded negotiation proposals.
criteria.counterevidence: None found; no unsupported claims, arithmetic errors, or contradictory instructions appear in the deliverable or trace.

criteria.rationale: The delivered Word document fulfills every substantive requirement of the prompt for an executive negotiation audience. It outlines a sincere preferred path to engage LPI on historical forecast underperformance and commercial grievances (Sections 1–2); defines negotiation levers including flexible delivery, secured advance payments, clean exit clauses, and non-exclusive residual or fleet volume alongside a conditional ZOPA (Section 3); analyzes alternative scenarios and an independent BATNA without conflating LPI bridge supply with an independent fallback (Section 4); provides a gated localization timeline and action plan covering parallel plastic (3–4 months) and electronics (4–5 months) streams and the ~25-day tooling transfer (Section 5); and establishes a diplomatic exit and tooling-recovery strategy that respects LPI's operational continuity and separates plastic tool ownership from electronics IP (Section 6). Unresolved operational assumptions are explicitly surfaced.

evidence.source_quote:
Create a 2–3-page negotiation strategy document in Word or PDF format. This document should:
•	Outline a preferred path to attempt resolution with LPI (despite the low probability), including LiIon’s responsibility to engage sincerely and understand the supplier’s issues.
•	Explore alternative scenarios and present a BATNA (Best Alternative to a Negotiated Agreement). Also mention the Zone Of Possible Agreement (ZOPA) for your strategy.
•	Lay out a viable timeline and action plan to transition the Modlev tail lamp to a local supplier if needed.
•	Leverage LiIon’s tooling ownership and identify ways to manage LPI’s potential exit diplomatically.
•	Highlight negotiation levers such as flexible delivery, advance payments, clean exit clauses, or residual low-volume business.
evidence.output_quote: The CPO should open by recognising LiIon’s responsibility to understand LPI’s concerns, including the commercial consequences of volumes repeatedly falling below pricing forecasts.

evidence.source_quote: •	Highlight negotiation levers such as flexible delivery, advance payments, clean exit clauses, or residual low-volume business.
evidence.output_quote: Trade certainty for continuity. Offer a realistic firm ordering window, agreed releases and flexible shipment frequency so LPI can run economic batches. Consider a time-limited bridge premium, milestone-linked advance payments, or settlement of validated claims in return for committed quantities, delivery dates and transition support.

evidence.source_quote: •	Explore alternative scenarios and present a BATNA (Best Alternative to a Negotiated Agreement). Also mention the Zone Of Possible Agreement (ZOPA) for your strategy.
evidence.output_quote: Scenario A: repair the relationship through revised economics and scheduling, while retaining an approved local second-source programme. Scenario B, the practical fallback: buy a defined LPI bridge and accelerate a local transition. Scenario C: if LPI refuses, execute the independent BATNA—secure verifiable finished stock and any authorised stock held by logistics partners or distributors, expedite qualified local development, and investigate already-qualified compatible alternatives.

evidence.source_quote: •	Leverage LiIon’s tooling ownership and identify ways to manage LPI’s potential exit diplomatically.
evidence.output_quote: Use LiIon’s paid-for plastic-tool ownership to request preservation, inspection, traceability and an agreed handover—not to imply immediate physical access or ownership of electronics IP.

criteria.consequence: None; the strategy document is complete and actionable for the executive negotiation session.
criteria.counterevidence: None found; all requested topics, constraints, and unresolved assumptions are addressed consistently.

task_defect.reason: The prompt and workspace records are internally consistent and clearly specify how to resolve the conflict between the approved 21-day notice record and the unapproved 84-day draft.

assessment.caveat: No weighted average can offset a critical failure. Exact quotes establish traceability, not entailment. Rendering and independent human calibration remain required.
